blindSummary: The sodomy/gross-indecency laws were struck down by the high court in July 2022, which read the constitutional bar on sex discrimination as covering sexual orientation and gender identity. No legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination statute, and residual social hostility; tourist resort areas are insulated.
blindOutOfScope: Decriminalisation is recent; social climate lags the courts.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust page documents constitutional challenges to laws criminalising same-sex activity across the region, including in this country.
An international human-rights group (Jul 2022): a regional supreme court ruling decriminalises consensual same-sex conduct in this country.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): in 2022 the high court found provisions of a 1995 sexual-offences act unconstitutional, decriminalising same-sex conduct, and interpreted 'sex' discrimination to include sexual orientation and gender identity. However, no explicit antidiscrimination protections exist, same-sex unions are not recognised, and trans people are particularly vulnerable because there is no mechanism to change legal gender markers - only name changes.

World-survey volume by an international LGBT association on laws prohibiting same-sex activity between consenting adults (May 2009): global survey with per-country entries; this country was then criminalising sodomy and gross indecency.

Foreign daily with a wire service (June 2023): profile of the local LGBTQ activist who challenged the country's anti-sodomy law and won in 2022 - bullied and physically attacked (struck in the head, knocked out in daylight); the regional court ruled the law unconstitutional; six states in the wider region still criminalise.

Regional newspaper (Dec 2019): an advocacy coalition announced court challenges to sodomy and indecency laws in five states of the region including this country, arguing the laws stigmatise and legitimise hate speech, discrimination and violence.
An international human-rights NGO: a treaty-body submission covering LGBTQ+ rights in this country.
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition and no anti-discrimination statute — resident-facing gaps.
blindTangential: The 2022 decriminalisation ruling covers same-sex conduct — relevant to trans visitors travelling with a partner; the criminal statutes no longer apply to anyone.
